title: Fix the delivery delay report
prompt: This report should show how many seconds each reading took to reach the platform, filed under the day it was measured, but two of its columns come out wrong. Fix `solve(sensor_readings)`.
rules: `reading_date` is the date of `event_time`, when the sensor measured (UTC).
`late_s` is `arrival_time` minus `event_time` as a whole number of seconds.
`status` comes from `payload.status` and `firmware_build` from `firmware.build`; a missing struct gives a missing value. Keep every reading.
hints: Run the starter and look at the type of `late_s` in the result. Is it a number?
Subtracting two timestamps gives a time interval, not seconds. The lesson cast each timestamp to `long` first.
Check which timestamp the date comes from. A reading measured at 23:58 can arrive after midnight.
explanation: Two bugs. Subtracting the timestamps directly gives an interval, so `late_s` had the wrong type; casting each one to `long` first gives seconds since 1970, and their difference is the delay in whole seconds: `F.col("arrival_time").cast("long") - F.col("event_time").cast("long")`. The date came from `arrival_time`, which files a reading measured just before midnight under the next day when it arrives late; `F.to_date("event_time")` uses the time it was measured. The struct paths for `status` and `firmware_build` were already right.
